title: brief-v4 frontmatter
description: Machine-readable contract for `schema: brief-v4` brief frontmatter. brief-v4 is brief-v3 plus the negotiated typed-reference surface: the `brief:` definition id is the full colon-only prefixed form `<cell>:<repo>:<stream>:b-<NN>`; the brief's own `version:` revision and its `id:` uuid are REQUIRED (no absent-means-1 default, no empty id); the optional `requires-milestones:` list carries exact versioned milestone start requirements (`<stream>:m-<NN>@<version>`, `<repo>:<stream>:m-<NN>@<version>` or `<cell>:<repo>:<stream>:m-<NN>@<version>`); and `depends:`/`unblocks:` entries may be written `<stream>:b-<NN>` with an optional exact `@<version>` brief-revision selector. Every brief-v3 rule applies unchanged. `depends`, `unblocks`, `outcome` and `satisfies` never name milestones. A brief-v4 record is written only after every required reader advertises brief-v4 syntax (the REQUIRED top-level `reader-requirements` envelope makes a reader that does not refuse the record); readers that do not advertise it must refuse rather than read the record through a legacy parser. Like brief-v1 to brief-v3 this contract is DESCRIPTIVE of the reference validator's per-file, frontmatter-shape rules only. It deliberately does NOT encode the cross-file rules the reference validator's `--lint` surface owns: the `brief:` id's stream/NN matching the file path, its cell and repo-alias segments and every milestone reference resolving in `docs/streams/graph-repos.yaml`, `id` uniqueness across the tree, exact revision binding of a pinned selector against the selected source snapshot (an unavailable revision is unknown, never substituted), duplicate or conflicting references, the wave/README agreement, the verifier floor and the risk-answer/gate coupling. Where the shape rule and the semantic rule would disagree the shape rule is the LOOSER of the two on purpose. Unknown top-level keys are tolerated (additionalProperties: true) exactly as the validator tolerates them; the `risk` block, each `parallel-streams` entry, each `gates`/`feathers` edge and each `verify` row are the closed objects the validator rejects unknown keys in.

schema.description: The opt-in schema marker. Its presence is what selects a file for validation; for this contract it is exactly brief-v4.

brief.description: The full colon-only prefixed brief definition id, `<cell>:<repo>:<stream>:b-<NN>` — no revision suffix and no slash. The cell and repo segments are aliases from docs/streams/graph-repos.yaml; RESOLVING them, and matching stream/NN against the file path, is the reference validator's job. The existing internal compatibility id `<cell>:<repo>:<stream>:<NN>` is derived from it, never authored here.

version.description: The brief's own authored revision counter (not the schema's, and not a milestone contract version): 1 at authoring, bumped on every edit to Task or Verify after first dispatch. REQUIRED under brief-v4 — a reference may pin it as `@<version>`, so it is never defaulted.

id.description: The stable object identity, a canonical uuid v4 minted ONCE at authoring and never reused. REQUIRED and non-empty under brief-v4: every alias and revision selector normalizes to this one identity, so no selector mints another.

supersedes.description: RESERVED (brief-v2): object lineage — the briefs this one splits or re-baselines, as references in the graph reference grammar. Optional; an empty list (or null) is allowed. Each ref's GRAMMAR and alias resolution is a `--lint` check, not a shape check.

gates.description: RESERVED, OPTIONAL-but-KNOWN (brief-v2): behavioural/ordering edges — parsed, type-checked and lint-validated, not yet gating. Every entry is a MAPPING; `on`, `type` and `reason` are all required, because the point of the field is the machine-attached why. No other key is allowed — a silently dropped key is an edge whose meaning nobody reads.

on.description: The edge target, in the graph reference grammar. Shape-checked as a non-empty string here; the grammar and alias resolution are `--lint` checks.

type.description: The edge taxonomy. A type outside this closed set is a PROBLEM rather than a silently dispatched-past edge.

reason.description: The machine-attached why for this edge.

feathers.description: RESERVED, OPTIONAL-but-KNOWN (brief-v2): cross-repo/cross-stream edges — the same reserved treatment as `gates`. An entry may be a bare reference STRING (which defaults to type build-dep with no reason) or a mapping carrying the why. In the mapping form `ref` is required and no key other than ref/type/reason is allowed.

ref.description: The edge target, in the graph reference grammar. Shape-checked as a non-empty string here; the grammar and alias resolution are `--lint` checks.

type.description: The edge taxonomy; absent in the mapping form it defaults to build-dep.

reason.description: The machine-attached why for this edge.

verify.description: RESERVED, OPTIONAL (brief-v2): per-Verify-row identity records. `id` names the row so a witness points at THE row it ran; `target` names the verify substrate when it is not this repo's tree (a sibling repo, a live cluster), turning the could-not-check-by-design class into a field instead of a NOTICE. Shape only; no other key is allowed.

wave.description: Dependency wave (a non-negative integer in practice; the validator type-checks integer only).

depends.description: Briefs this brief depends on, in this root: `<stream>:b-<NN>` (canonical for new writes) with an optional exact `@<version>` selector, or a legacy `<stream>/<NN>` / `<stream>:<NN>` compatibility form. Each brief is named once. Never a milestone reference. An empty list (or null) is allowed.

unblocks.description: Briefs this brief unblocks, in the same forms as `depends`. Never a milestone reference. An empty list (or null) is allowed.

requires-milestones.description: OPTIONAL milestone start requirements: exact versioned milestone references (`<stream>:m-<NN>@<version>`, `<repo>:<stream>:m-<NN>@<version>` or `<cell>:<repo>:<stream>:m-<NN>@<version>`). A present entry means that milestone's capability must be accepted before this brief starts; a reader that cannot evaluate it holds the brief as could-not-check, never ready. Absent or empty means no additional milestone start requirement.

reader-requirements.description: REQUIRED under brief-v4: the top-level reader-requirements envelope (reader-requirements-v1). It must require `syntax` support for `brief-v4`, so that a reader whose advertisement lists only the legacy schemas assesses it unsupported and refuses the record. A record without the envelope is read as a legacy record by a reader that checks only envelopes, so the envelope is never optional. The reference validator also checks that the declared requirement holds back a legacy-only reader; the shape rule here is the looser of the two.

risk.description: The four canonical risk questions. All four are required, each answered exactly `yes` or `no` (bare YAML strings, not booleans), and no other key is allowed.

issues.description: Tracking issue numbers. An empty list (or null) is allowed.

authored.description: Authoring provenance. Required to be present; the reference validator enforces presence only, not a fixed type (a bare date and a free-text line are both accepted).

gate-why.description: Optional rationale for a risk-gated brief.

value.description: Optional worth signal; absence defaults to med at scoring time.

domain.description: Optional Cynefin domain; absence defaults to complicated at read time.

exec-tier.description: Optional minimum execution-model tier; absence defaults to any.

exec-tier-why.description: Optional one-line rationale for exec-tier: strong.

blocked-by.description: Optional environment-blocked marker; absence means not blocked.

measures.description: Optional name of the process queue this brief instruments; a present value must name a wired queue.

homed-in.description: Optional `<owner>/<repo>` the deliverable was re-homed to; absence means a normal in-repo brief.

consumers.description: Optional routed reader list (a list of strings) or a prose paragraph (a single string).

parallel-streams.description: Optional declared shards of an intra-brief split. Only name and files are defined per entry; any other key is rejected. Shape only — whether the split is safe to dispatch is decided elsewhere.

decision-issue.description: Optional GitHub issue number tracking a human decision on this brief.

ruling.description: Optional link to the comment on decision-issue that records the human ruling, as an issue-comment URL (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<N>#issuecomment-<ID>). Only the type is a shape rule; the link's grammar and what it must resolve to are the gate:human transition check's (lifecycle-v1 section 4.5).

independence-override.description: Optional recorded, human-authorized override of the committer-identity independence check for this one brief, as "human:<name> YYYY-MM-DD <reason>". Only the type is a shape rule; the grammar, the named human and the commit that recorded it are judged by the reference validator's --lint independence check.

withdrawn-date.description: Optional on a live brief only in the sense that the shape allows it; REQUIRED when the README Status cell is `withdrawn`: the YYYY-MM-DD date the brief was withdrawn. Only the type is a shape rule; the date grammar and the pairing with the README `withdrawn` status are the reference validator's `--lint` rules.

withdrawn-reason.description: REQUIRED and non-empty when the README Status cell is `withdrawn`: one sentence saying why the brief was withdrawn and what, if anything, survives where.

superseded-by.description: The successor list of a withdrawn brief: `<stream>/<NN>` ids in this repo, or global `<cell>:<repo-alias>:<stream>:<NN>` ids for another repo. An empty list means won't-fix (no successor). Same-repo ids must resolve; global ids are syntax-checked and resolved only when the named root is configured — `--lint` rules, not shape rules.

withdrawal-context.description: Optional shared, revision-bound amendment provenance. Lint reads the local handoff, checks its canonical digest, approval revision, subject, action, successors, preserved history and active-work acknowledgement. Never clears execution drift.
